correctness.rationale: Bézout supplies reduced projective complete intersection of degree m²; degree-m part of its saturated ideal has basis P,Q. A nontrivial companion gives a nonscalar constant matrix, hence a nonzero quadratic differential operator. Its distinct-characteristic case yields separation; its repeated-characteristic case yields at most m nondegenerate points, contradicting m² for m≥2. The converse and all companions follow from elementary integration.
